framework.name: Common Core State Standards — Mathematics (K–8 + HS)
framework.subject: MATH
framework.description: CCSS Mathematics coverage pack: Kindergarten–Grade 8 plus High School Algebra, Geometry, and Statistics samples.

metadata.note: Merged former ccss-math-g5 into this pack as GRADE G5.

children.title: Count to 100 by ones and by tens
children.summary: Count to 100 by ones and by tens.

objectives.statement: Students count aloud to 100 by ones and by tens.
objectives.masteryCriteria: Accurate count by ones to 20 and by tens to 100.

children.title: Understand the relationship between numbers and quantities
children.summary: Understand that the last number name said tells the number of objects counted.

objectives.statement: Students count a set and state how many without recounting.

children.title: Count forward from a given number
children.summary: Count forward beginning from a given number.

objectives.statement: Students continue a count from a given start.

children.title: Identify whether a group has more/fewer/equal
children.summary: Identify whether the number of objects in one group is greater than, less than, or equal to another.

objectives.statement: Students compare two groups using matching or counting.

children.title: Represent addition and subtraction with objects
children.summary: Represent addition and subtraction with objects, fingers, drawings.

objectives.statement: Students model +/− within 10 with objects.

children.title: Solve addition and subtraction word problems within 10
children.summary: Solve addition and subtraction word problems within 10.

objectives.statement: Students solve a within-10 word problem.

children.title: Describe objects using shape names and position
children.summary: Describe objects using names of shapes and relative positions.

objectives.statement: Students name a shape and its position.

children.title: Analyze and compare 2D and 3D shapes
children.summary: Analyze and compare two- and three-dimensional shapes.

objectives.statement: Students sort shapes by attributes.

children.title: Solve addition and subtraction word problems within 20
children.summary: Use addition and subtraction within 20 to solve word problems.

objectives.statement: Students solve a word problem with a matching equation and answer.
objectives.masteryCriteria: Correct equation + answer for 4 of 5 items.

children.title: Add and subtract within 20 using strategies
children.summary: Add and subtract within 20, demonstrating fluency within 10.

objectives.statement: Students compute within 20 using a named strategy.

children.title: Apply properties of operations
children.summary: Apply properties of operations as strategies to add and subtract.

objectives.statement: Students use commutative/associative ideas informally.

children.title: Determine the unknown in an equation
children.summary: Determine the unknown whole number in an addition or subtraction equation.

objectives.statement: Students find the missing number in □ equations.

children.title: Count to 120 and represent numerals
children.summary: Count to 120 starting at any number less than 120.

objectives.statement: Students count on and write numerals to 120.

children.title: Understand tens and ones
children.summary: Understand that the two digits of a two-digit number represent tens and ones.

objectives.statement: Students decompose a teen/two-digit number into tens and ones.

children.title: Add within 100 using place value
children.summary: Add within 100 using concrete models or drawings and strategies based on place value.

objectives.statement: Students add two-digit + one-digit or multiple of 10.

children.title: Understand hundreds, tens, and ones
children.summary: Understand that the three digits of a three-digit number represent amounts of hundreds, tens, and ones.

objectives.statement: Students identify place values in a 3-digit number.
objectives.masteryCriteria: Correct place-value breakdown for 4 of 5 numbers.

children.title: Fluently add and subtract within 100
children.summary: Fluently add and subtract within 100 using strategies based on place value.

objectives.statement: Students add/subtract within 100 with a place-value strategy.

children.title: Compare three-digit numbers
children.summary: Compare two three-digit numbers based on meanings of the hundreds, tens, and ones digits.

objectives.statement: Students compare with >, =, < and place-value reason.

children.title: Add and subtract within 1000
children.summary: Add and subtract within 1000 using concrete models or drawings and strategies.

objectives.statement: Students compute a within-1000 problem with a model/strategy.

children.title: Solve one- and two-step word problems within 100
children.summary: Use addition and subtraction within 100 to solve one- and two-step word problems.

objectives.statement: Students solve a two-step within-100 problem.

children.title: Fluently add and subtract within 20
children.summary: Fluently add and subtract within 20 using mental strategies.

objectives.statement: Students compute within 20 fluently.

children.title: Use addition to find total of equal groups
children.summary: Use addition to find the total number of objects in rectangular arrays.

objectives.statement: Students write an addition equation for an array.

children.title: Measure length with appropriate tools
children.summary: Measure the length of an object by selecting and using appropriate tools.

objectives.statement: Students measure with ruler/meter stick appropriately.

children.title: Draw a picture/bar graph and solve problems
children.summary: Draw a picture graph and a bar graph to represent data; solve problems.

objectives.statement: Students build a bar graph and answer 2 questions.

children.title: Understand a fraction 1/b as the quantity formed by 1 part
children.summary: Understand a fraction 1/b as the quantity formed by 1 part when a whole is partitioned into b equal parts.

objectives.statement: Students shade 1/b of a model and name the unit fraction.
objectives.masteryCriteria: Correct model + name for 3 of 3 prompts.

children.title: Explain equivalence of fractions and compare
children.summary: Explain equivalence of fractions in special cases and compare fractions by reasoning about their size.

objectives.statement: Students justify why two fractions are equivalent or which is larger.
objectives.masteryCriteria: Correct comparison with reason for 4 of 5 items.

children.title: Represent fractions on a number line
children.summary: Understand a fraction as a number on the number line.

objectives.statement: Students locate a/b on a number line.

children.title: Interpret products of whole numbers
children.summary: Interpret products of whole numbers as equal groups.

objectives.statement: Students relate a×b to equal groups.

children.title: Solve multiplication/division word problems within 100
children.summary: Use multiplication and division within 100 to solve word problems.

objectives.statement: Students solve a ×/÷ word problem within 100.

children.title: Fluently multiply and divide within 100
children.summary: Fluently multiply and divide within 100.

objectives.statement: Students compute ×/÷ within 100 fluently.

children.title: Solve two-step word problems using four operations
children.summary: Solve two-step word problems using the four operations.

objectives.statement: Students solve a two-step mixed-operation problem.

children.title: Tell and write time to the nearest minute
children.summary: Tell and write time to the nearest minute and measure time intervals.

objectives.statement: Students read/write time and solve an elapsed-time problem.

children.title: Relate area to multiplication and addition
children.summary: Relate area to the operations of multiplication and addition.

objectives.statement: Students find area of a rectangle using tiling or a×b.

metadata.cluster: Use the four operations with whole numbers to solve problems

children.title: Use the four operations with whole numbers to solve problems
children.titleKo: 네 가지 연산을 사용해 자연수 문제 해결

children.title: Interpret multiplicative comparison equations
children.summary: Interpret a multiplication equation as a comparison, e.g., interpret 35 = 5 × 7 as a statement that 35 is 5 times as many as 7 and 7 times as many as 5.

objectives.statement: Students explain a multiplication equation as a multiplicative comparison using language such as “times as many.”
objectives.statementKo: 곱셈식을 “몇 배만큼” 등의 언어로 곱셈적 비교로 설명한다.
objectives.masteryCriteria: Given 3 comparison situations, student correctly matches each to a multiplication equation and explains using “times as many” language.
objectives.masteryCriteriaKo: 비교 상황 3개를 곱셈식과 연결하고 “몇 배” 언어로 설명한다.

objectives.statement: Students represent verbal multiplicative comparisons with equations using a symbol for the unknown.
objectives.statementKo: 말과 글로 된 곱셈적 비교를 미지수 기호가 있는 식으로 나타낸다.
objectives.masteryCriteria: Student writes a correct equation with unknown for 4/5 verbal comparison prompts.

children.title: Multiply or divide to solve multiplicative comparison word problems
children.summary: Multiply or divide to solve word problems involving multiplicative comparison, e.g., by using drawings and equations with a symbol for the unknown number.

objectives.statement: Students solve one-step multiplicative comparison word problems using multiplication or division and represent with a drawing or equation.
objectives.masteryCriteria: ≥80% accuracy on a 10-item formative set mixing “times as many” multiply and divide cases.

children.title: Solve multistep word problems with whole numbers
children.summary: Solve multistep word problems posed with whole numbers and having whole-number answers using the four operations, including problems in which remainders must be interpreted.

objectives.statement: Students solve multistep word problems using the four operations and interpret remainders in context.
objectives.masteryCriteria: Student correctly solves and explains remainder meaning in at least 2 of 3 contextual remainder problems.

children.title: Gain familiarity with factors and multiples
Find factor pairs; identify primes and composites
children.titleKo: 약수 쌍 찾기; 소수와 합성수 구분하기
children.summary: Find all factor pairs for a whole number in the range 1–100. Recognize that a whole number is a multiple of each of its factors. Determine whether a given whole number in the range 1–100 is prime or composite.

objectives.statement: Students list all factor pairs for numbers ≤100 and classify numbers as prime or composite.
objectives.masteryCriteria: Correct factor pairs for 8/10 numbers; correct prime/composite for 9/10.

children.title: Generalize place value understanding for multi-digit whole numbers
children.titleKo: 여러 자리 자연수의 자릿값 이해 일반화

children.title: Recognize place value relationships (10 times)
children.summary: Recognize that in a multi-digit whole number, a digit in one place represents ten times what it represents in the place to its right.

objectives.statement: Students explain that a digit in one place is ten times the value of the same digit one place to the right.
objectives.masteryCriteria: Student explains place-value ×10 relationship with a correct example for 3 of 3 prompts.

children.title: Read, write, and compare multi-digit whole numbers
children.titleKo: 여러 자리 자연수 읽고 쓰고 비교하기
children.summary: Read and write multi-digit whole numbers using base-ten numerals, number names, and expanded form. Compare two multi-digit numbers based on meanings of the digits in each place.

objectives.statement: Students write numbers in standard, word, and expanded form and compare using place value.

children.title: Extend understanding of fraction equivalence and ordering
Explain why fractions are equivalent using visual models
children.summary: Explain why a fraction a/b is equivalent to a fraction (n×a)/(n×b) by using visual fraction models.

objectives.statement: Students generate and justify an equivalent fraction with a visual model.
objectives.masteryCriteria: Produces a correct equivalent pair and cites a model for 2 of 2 prompts.

children.title: Compare two fractions with different numerators and denominators
children.summary: Compare two fractions with different numerators and different denominators by creating common denominators or numerators, or by comparing to a benchmark.

objectives.statement: Students compare fractions using a common denominator or benchmark and record with >, =, or <.
objectives.masteryCriteria: ≥80% accuracy on 8 comparison items with a stated strategy.

children.title: Understand a fraction a/b as a sum of unit fractions 1/b
children.summary: Understand a fraction a/b with a > 1 as a sum of fractions 1/b.

objectives.statement: Students decompose a fraction into unit fractions and record an equation.
objectives.masteryCriteria: Correct decomposition equation + model for 3 of 3 fractions.

children.title: Multiply a fraction by a whole number
children.summary: Apply and extend previous understandings of multiplication to multiply a fraction by a whole number.

objectives.statement: Students solve n × (a/b) problems using models or equations.

children.title: Know relative sizes of measurement units
children.summary: Know relative sizes of measurement units within one system.

objectives.statement: Students convert between related units within a system.

children.title: Apply area and perimeter formulas for rectangles
children.summary: Apply the area and perimeter formulas for rectangles in real-world problems.

objectives.statement: Students solve an area/perimeter application.

children.title: Recognize angles as geometric shapes
children.summary: Recognize angles as geometric shapes formed when two rays share an endpoint.

objectives.statement: Students identify and sketch angles.

children.title: Draw points, lines, rays, and angles
children.summary: Draw points, lines, line segments, rays, angles, and perpendicular/parallel lines.

objectives.statement: Students draw and label geometric figures.

children.title: Classify figures by properties of lines and angles
children.summary: Classify two-dimensional figures based on presence of parallel/perpendicular lines or angles.

objectives.statement: Students classify shapes by line/angle properties.

children.title: Recognize that a digit in one place represents 10 times as much
children.summary: Recognize that in a multi-digit number, a digit in one place represents 10 times as much as it represents in the place to its right and 1/10 of what it represents in the place to its left.

objectives.statement: Students explain ×10 / ÷10 place-value relationships across adjacent places, including decimals.
objectives.masteryCriteria: Correct explanations for 4/5 adjacent-place prompts including tenths/hundredths.

children.title: Read, write, and compare decimals to thousandths
children.summary: Read, write, and compare decimals to thousandths.

objectives.statement: Students read/write decimals to thousandths and compare using place value.
objectives.masteryCriteria: ≥85% on mixed read/write/compare formative including thousandths.

children.title: Use place value to round decimals to any place
children.summary: Use place value understanding to round decimals to any place.

objectives.statement: Students round decimals to a specified place using place-value reasoning.
objectives.masteryCriteria: Correct rounding on 8/10 items across tenths–thousandths.

children.title: Use equivalent fractions as a strategy to add and subtract fractions
Add and subtract fractions with unlike denominators
children.summary: Add and subtract fractions with unlike denominators (including mixed numbers) by replacing given fractions with equivalent fractions.

objectives.statement: Students add/subtract fractions with unlike denominators using equivalent fractions.
objectives.masteryCriteria: ≥80% on 8 mixed add/subtract items with unlike denominators.

children.title: Multiply a fraction or whole number by a fraction
children.summary: Apply and extend previous understandings of multiplication to multiply a fraction or whole number by a fraction.

objectives.statement: Students multiply fractions and interpret products with a model or equation.
objectives.masteryCriteria: Correct product + interpretation for 4 of 5 prompts.

children.title: Use parentheses/brackets in numerical expressions
children.summary: Use parentheses, brackets, or braces in numerical expressions and evaluate.

objectives.statement: Students evaluate expressions with grouping symbols.

children.title: Write and interpret simple expressions
children.summary: Write simple expressions that record calculations and interpret without evaluating.

objectives.statement: Students write an expression from a verbal phrase.

children.title: Convert among different-sized measurement units
children.summary: Convert among different-sized standard measurement units within a system.

objectives.statement: Students convert and use conversions in multi-step problems.

children.title: Relate volume to multiplication and addition
children.summary: Relate volume to the operations of multiplication and addition; solve real-world problems.

objectives.statement: Students find volume of a rectangular prism.

children.title: Use a coordinate plane in the first quadrant
children.summary: Use a pair of perpendicular number lines to define a coordinate system.

objectives.statement: Students plot and name points in quadrant I.

children.title: Understand categories of 2D figures
children.summary: Understand that attributes belonging to a category of two-dimensional figures also belong to all subcategories.

objectives.statement: Students explain a hierarchy (e.g., rectangles/squares).

children.title: Understand the concept of a ratio
children.summary: Understand the concept of a ratio and use ratio language to describe a ratio relationship between two quantities.

objectives.statement: Students write a ratio and describe the relationship in words.
objectives.masteryCriteria: Correct ratio language for 3 of 3 scenarios.

children.title: Use ratio and rate reasoning to solve problems
children.summary: Use ratio and rate reasoning to solve real-world and mathematical problems.

objectives.statement: Students solve a rate/ratio problem with a table or equation.
objectives.masteryCriteria: Correct solution + representation for 4 of 5 items.

children.title: Understand positive and negative numbers
children.summary: Understand that positive and negative numbers are used together to describe quantities having opposite directions or values.

objectives.statement: Students place integers on a number line and interpret a real-world signed quantity.

children.title: Write, read, and evaluate expressions
children.summary: Write, read, and evaluate expressions in which letters stand for numbers.

objectives.statement: Students evaluate an algebraic expression for given values.

children.title: Understand solving equations as a process
children.summary: Understand solving an equation or inequality as a process of answering which values make it true.

objectives.statement: Students test values and solve a one-step equation.

children.title: Solve real-world equations of form x+p=q and px=q
children.titleKo: x+p=q, px=q 형태 실생활 방정식 풀기
children.summary: Solve real-world and mathematical problems by writing and solving equations of the form x+p=q and px=q.

objectives.statement: Students write and solve a one-step equation from context.

children.title: Find area of triangles and special quadrilaterals
children.summary: Find the area of right triangles, other triangles, special quadrilaterals, and polygons.

objectives.statement: Students compute area by composing/decomposing shapes.

children.title: Find volume of a right rectangular prism with fractional edges
children.summary: Find the volume of a right rectangular prism with fractional edge lengths.

objectives.statement: Students compute V=lwh with fractional edges.

children.title: Recognize a statistical question
children.summary: Recognize a statistical question as one that anticipates variability.

objectives.statement: Students distinguish statistical vs non-statistical questions.

children.title: Summarize numerical data sets
children.summary: Summarize numerical data sets in relation to their context.

objectives.statement: Students report center/spread for a data set.

children.title: Recognize and represent proportional relationships
children.summary: Recognize and represent proportional relationships between quantities.

objectives.statement: Students identify a proportional relationship and write an equation y=kx.
objectives.masteryCriteria: Correct constant of proportionality for 4 of 5 tables.

children.title: Use variables to represent quantities in real-world problems
children.summary: Use variables to represent quantities and construct simple equations and inequalities.

objectives.statement: Students write and solve a one-variable equation for a word problem.
objectives.masteryCriteria: Correct equation + solution for 4 of 5 items.

children.title: Solve real-world problems with rational numbers
children.summary: Solve real-world and mathematical problems involving the four operations with rational numbers.

objectives.statement: Students compute with signed rationals in a multi-step context.

children.title: Apply and extend addition/subtraction to rational numbers
children.summary: Apply and extend previous understandings of addition and subtraction to add and subtract rational numbers.

objectives.statement: Students add/subtract signed rationals on a number line or with rules.

children.title: Multiply and divide rational numbers
children.summary: Apply and extend previous understandings of multiplication and division of fractions to multiply and divide rational numbers.

objectives.statement: Students multiply/divide signed rationals.

children.title: Solve problems involving scale drawings
children.summary: Solve problems involving scale drawings of geometric figures.

objectives.statement: Students use a scale factor to find a missing length.

children.title: Know formulas for area/circumference of a circle
children.summary: Know the formulas for the area and circumference of a circle and use them to solve problems.

objectives.statement: Students compute circumference or area given r or d.

children.title: Solve real-world problems involving area, volume, surface area
children.summary: Solve real-world and mathematical problems involving area, volume, and surface area of 2D/3D objects.

objectives.statement: Students solve a composite area or prism volume problem.

children.title: Understand statistics from random sampling
children.summary: Understand that statistics can be used to gain information about a population by examining a sample.

objectives.statement: Students explain why a sample may/may not represent a population.

children.title: Understand probability of a chance event
children.summary: Understand that the probability of a chance event is a number between 0 and 1.

objectives.statement: Students assign approximate probabilities and justify.

children.title: Understand that a function assigns exactly one output
children.summary: Understand that a function is a rule that assigns to each input exactly one output.

objectives.statement: Students decide whether a relation is a function and justify.
objectives.masteryCriteria: Correct function/non-function decisions for 4 of 5 relations.

children.title: Graph proportional relationships and interpret slope
children.titleKo: 비례 관계를 그래프로 그리고 기울기 해석하기
children.summary: Graph proportional relationships, interpreting the unit rate as the slope.

objectives.statement: Students graph y=kx and interpret slope as unit rate.
objectives.masteryCriteria: Correct graph + slope interpretation for 3 of 3.

children.title: Apply the Pythagorean Theorem
children.summary: Apply the Pythagorean Theorem to determine unknown side lengths in right triangles.

objectives.statement: Students find a missing side using a²+b²=c².
objectives.masteryCriteria: Correct missing side for 4 of 5 right triangles.

children.title: Know that there are irrational numbers
children.summary: Know that numbers that are not rational are called irrational.

objectives.statement: Students classify numbers as rational/irrational with reason.

children.title: Approximate irrational numbers
children.summary: Use rational approximations of irrational numbers to compare size and locate on a number line.

objectives.statement: Students approximate √n between integers.

children.title: Know and apply properties of integer exponents
children.summary: Know and apply the properties of integer exponents to generate equivalent expressions.

objectives.statement: Students simplify expressions with integer exponents.

children.title: Solve linear equations in one variable
children.summary: Solve linear equations in one variable.

objectives.statement: Students solve multi-step linear equations.

children.title: Analyze and solve pairs of simultaneous linear equations
children.summary: Analyze and solve pairs of simultaneous linear equations.

objectives.statement: Students solve a 2×2 system algebraically or graphically.

children.title: Construct and interpret scatter plots
children.summary: Construct and interpret scatter plots for bivariate measurement data to investigate patterns of association.

objectives.statement: Students describe association in a scatter plot.
objectives.masteryCriteria: Correct association description for 2 of 2 plots.

children.title: Informally fit a straight line to scatter data
children.summary: Know that straight lines are used to model relationships between two quantitative variables.

objectives.statement: Students sketch a line of best fit and interpret slope informally.

children.title: Solve linear equations and inequalities in one variable
children.summary: Solve linear equations and inequalities in one variable, including equations with coefficients represented by letters.

objectives.statement: Students solve a linear equation/inequality and check the solution.
objectives.masteryCriteria: Correct solution set for 4 of 5 items.

children.title: Solve systems of linear equations exactly and approximately
children.summary: Solve systems of linear equations exactly and approximately (e.g., with graphs).

objectives.statement: Students solve a 2×2 system algebraically and verify graphically.
objectives.masteryCriteria: Correct solution + verification for 3 of 3 systems.

children.title: Understand graph of an equation as solution set
children.summary: Understand that the graph of an equation in two variables is the set of all its solutions plotted.

objectives.statement: Students explain why a point is/isn't on a graph.

children.title: Interpret expressions in context
children.summary: Interpret expressions that represent a quantity in terms of its context.

objectives.statement: Students interpret parts of an expression in a model.

children.title: Use structure to rewrite expressions
children.summary: Use the structure of an expression to identify ways to rewrite it.

objectives.statement: Students factor or rewrite using structure.

children.title: Understand function concept and notation
children.summary: Understand that a function assigns each element of the domain exactly one output.

objectives.statement: Students evaluate f(x) and explain domain/range.

children.title: Interpret key features of graphs and tables
children.summary: For a function, interpret key features of graphs and tables in terms of quantities.

objectives.statement: Students identify intercepts, intervals of increase, maxima.

children.title: Graph functions and show key features
children.titleKo: 함수 그래프 그리고 핵심 특징 보이기
children.summary: Graph functions expressed symbolically and show key features of the graph.

objectives.statement: Students graph a linear/quadratic and label key features.

children.title: Know precise definitions of angle, circle, etc.
children.summary: Know precise definitions of angle, circle, perpendicular line, parallel line, and line segment.

objectives.statement: Students state precise definitions.

children.title: Use rigid motions to transform figures
children.summary: Use geometric descriptions of rigid motions to transform figures and predict effect.

objectives.statement: Students describe a rigid motion taking one figure onto another.

children.title: Prove theorems about lines and angles
children.summary: Prove theorems about lines and angles.

objectives.statement: Students complete a proof about vertical/corresponding angles.

children.title: Given two figures, use definition of similarity
children.summary: Given two figures, use the definition of similarity in terms of similarity transformations.

objectives.statement: Students decide similarity and cite correspondence.

children.title: Understand trigonometric ratios for acute angles
children.summary: Understand that by similarity, side ratios in right triangles are properties of the angles.

objectives.statement: Students define sin/cos/tan for an acute angle.

children.title: Use trigonometric ratios to solve right triangles
children.summary: Use trigonometric ratios and the Pythagorean Theorem to solve right triangles in applied problems.

objectives.statement: Students solve for a missing side/angle in context.

children.title: Represent data with plots on the real number line
children.summary: Represent data with plots on the real number line (dot plots, histograms, box plots).

objectives.statement: Students create an appropriate plot for a data set.

children.title: Represent bivariate data on a scatter plot
children.summary: Represent data on two quantitative variables on a scatter plot and describe how variables are related.

objectives.statement: Students describe form, direction, strength.

children.title: Interpret slope and intercept of a linear model
children.summary: Interpret the slope and the intercept of a linear model in the context of the data.

objectives.statement: Students interpret slope/intercept in context.
